item.title: Does the European Union's digital lifeline stay afloat?
item.description:
This summer, children in Europe will be safer and better protected during their vacations. At least, that is the European Commission’s goal. It’s not about handing out sunscreen or stationing lifeguards on Mediterranean beaches. In this case, the European Union’s executive body will seek to keep them away from their smartphone screens.

The conversation about protecting children online is moving at a dramatic pace. Following Australia’s lead—which in December 2025 banned the use of social media by minors under 16—more and more countries have decided to take a similar path. In our region, Brazil enacted and regulated the Digital Statute for Children and Adolescents (ECA Digital), which we have already discussed here. In Europe, Austria and Poland, among others, are seeking to require large internet platforms to verify the age of their users. The United Kingdom also announced a ban on social media use by minors under 16, effective in January.
